title: Suicide Risk, Psychiatric Conditions and Safe Restraint

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already manage overdoses, control bleeding and work beside police on violent scenes. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Assess suicide risk step by step, and act on it
  2. Recognize panic, depression, mania and psychosis, and their medical mimics
  3. De-escalate, then restrain safely, without positional asphyxia

Textbook: Chapter 40, PDF pages 3433–3470
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, you've already treated overdoses, controlled bleeding from self-inflicted wounds, and worked beside police on violent scenes. Today we go deeper. First, how to ask about suicide, step by step, and what to do with the answers. Second, how to recognize panic, depression, mania, and psychosis, and the medical problems that hide behind them. Third, how to calm an angry patient with words and, when words fail, how to restrain safely, so nobody dies from being held in the wrong position.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，你们已经处理过过量，控制过自伤造成的出血，也在暴力现场和警察并肩工作过。今天再深入一层。第一，怎样一步步询问自杀问题，以及根据回答怎么做。第二，怎样识别惊恐、抑郁、躁狂和精神病，以及藏在它们背后的躯体问题。第三，怎样用语言让愤怒的病人平静下来；语言无效时，怎样安全地约束，不让任何人因为被按在错误的体位而死亡。

slides.title: Panic attack, or something worse?
slides.body:
• Sudden terror + autonomic surge: racing heart, sweating, shaking
  • Chest pain, choking, tingling, dizziness, fear of dying
  • Peaks in about 10 minutes, lasts about 1 hour
  • Mimics: dysrhythmia, withdrawal, anaphylaxis, overactive thyroid
  • No paper bag: coach slow breathing
  • First attack? Full hospital assessment
slides.say: A panic attack is a sudden wave of terror with a massive surge of the autonomic nervous system: a racing heart, sweating, shaking, chest pain, choking, tingling, and a fear of dying. It usually peaks in about ten minutes and lasts about an hour. Calm the scene and use the word safe. But be careful: a dysrhythmia, withdrawal, anaphylaxis, or an overactive thyroid can look just like panic. Never use a paper bag; if the real cause is a pulmonary embolism or a heart problem, rebreathing can cause deadly hypoxia. Coach slower breathing instead. And a first attack always needs a full hospital assessment.
slides.sayZh: 惊恐发作是突然袭来的强烈恐惧，伴随自主神经系统的大量放电：心跳飞快、出汗、发抖、胸痛、哽噎感、发麻，还有濒死感。通常约十分钟达到高峰，持续约一小时。让现场安静下来，多用「安全」这个词。但要小心：心律失常、戒断、过敏反应或甲状腺功能亢进，都可能和惊恐一模一样。绝不要用纸袋；如果真正的原因是肺栓塞或心脏问题，回吸会造成致命的低氧。改为指导病人放慢呼吸。第一次发作一定要送医院全面评估。

slides.title: Depression: GAS PIPES
slides.body:
Gguilt, feeling worthless
Aappetite change, usually less
Ssleep: wakes at 3 or 4 a.m.
Ppaying attention is hard
Iinterest in old pleasures gone
Ppsychomotor: slowed or agitated
Eenergy gone
Ssuicidal thoughts keep returning

A sudden improvement is a suicide risk factor, not good news.
slides.say: Depression is more than sadness; it's the leading cause of disability between ages fifteen and forty-four. The memory aid is GAS PIPES. G, guilt and feeling worthless. A, appetite change, usually less. S, sleep trouble, classically waking at three or four in the morning. P, paying attention is hard. I, interest in old pleasures is gone. P, psychomotor change, slowed down or restless. E, no energy. S, suicidal thoughts that keep coming back. One trap: if a long-depressed patient suddenly seems calm and much better, don't relax. Sudden improvement is a listed suicide risk factor.
slides.sayZh: 抑郁不只是难过，它是十五到四十四岁人群致残的首要原因。口诀是 GAS PIPES。G，内疚、觉得自己没价值；A，食欲改变，通常是减退；S，睡眠障碍，典型是凌晨三四点醒来；P，注意力难以集中；I，对过去喜欢的事失去兴趣；P，精神运动改变，变慢或坐立不安；E，没有精力；S，反复出现的自杀念头。有个陷阱：长期抑郁的病人如果突然显得平静、好了很多，不要放松。突然好转本身就被列为自杀危险因素。

slides.title: Suicide: who is at highest risk?
slides.body:
• Past attempt: over half of those who die tried before
  • Three in four gave a clear warning
  • A concrete plan and the means to carry it out
  • Depression (or sudden improvement), alcohol or drugs, schizophrenia
  • Recent loss, job or money trouble, isolation, chronic illness
  • Family history; men under 55; single, widowed or divorced
slides.say: Suicide is the third leading cause of death from ages fifteen to twenty-five, and the fourth from twenty-five to forty-four. Women attempt it more often; men die from it more often. About one in six people with depression will eventually take their own life. Two numbers should change how you listen: more than half of those who die had tried before, and three in four gave a clear warning. Other big risk factors are a concrete plan with the means, alcohol or drugs, a recent loss, money or job trouble, isolation, and a family history of suicide.
slides.sayZh: 自杀是十五到二十五岁人群的第三大死因，二十五到四十四岁的第四大死因。女性尝试更多，男性死亡更多。约六分之一的抑郁症病人最终死于自杀。有两个数字会改变你倾听的方式：自杀死亡者超过一半以前尝试过，四分之三曾发出明确预警。其他重要危险因素有：有具体计划且有手段、酒精或药物、近期丧失、经济或失业问题、社交孤立，以及自杀家族史。

slides.title: Ask directly, step by step
slides.body:
Life worth living?→Wished to be dead?→Thoughts of self-harm?→Right now?
A plan?→The means?→Family history?→Past attempts?

Asking does not plant the idea; most patients feel relief. Past attempt, concrete plan or suicide in close family → hospital assessment.
slides.say: Many paramedics avoid asking about suicide because they fear it will give the patient the idea. It won't. A depressed patient has usually thought about it already, and most feel relieved when someone finally asks. Go step by step, from general to specific: whether life still feels worth living, whether they've wished they were dead, whether they've thought of harming themselves, and whether they feel that way now. Then the details: a plan, the means, suicide in the family, and past attempts. A past attempt, a concrete plan, or suicide in a close relative means high risk and a hospital assessment.
slides.sayZh: 很多救护员不敢问自杀，怕问了反而让病人起念头。不会的。抑郁病人通常早就想过，大多数人在终于有人问起时反而松了口气。从一般到具体，一步步问：是否还觉得活着有意义，是否希望自己死了，是否想过伤害自己，现在是否还这么想。然后问细节：有没有计划、有没有手段、家里有没有人自杀过、自己以前试过没有。既往尝试、具体计划或近亲自杀史，都意味着高风险，必须送医院评估。

slides.q: A 70-year-old man, depressed since his wife died, now seems calm. He says he 'feels at peace' and won't 'be a bother much longer'. He lives alone and declines help. What should you do next?
options: Accept that he's improving and leave with advice
Ask him directly about suicidal thoughts, a plan and the means
Avoid the topic so you don't put the idea in his head
Ask his daughter to book a doctor's visit next week
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A seventy-year-old man, depressed since his wife died, now seems calm. He says he feels at peace and won't be a bother much longer. He lives alone and declines help. What should you do next? A, accept that he's improving and leave with advice. B, ask him directly about suicidal thoughts, a plan, and the means. C, avoid the topic so you don't put the idea in his head. D, ask his daughter to book a doctor's visit next week. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。一位七十岁男性，妻子去世后一直抑郁，现在显得很平静。他说自己「心里很平和」，「不会再麻烦大家多久了」。他独居，拒绝帮助。下一步你该怎么做？A 认为他在好转，给些建议后离开；B 直接询问他有没有自杀念头、计划和手段；C 避开这个话题，免得让他起念头；D 让他女儿下周给他约医生。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A sudden calm after long depression is a risk factor, and not being a bother much longer sounds like a warning. He's also widowed and isolated. Ask directly, step by step, about thoughts, a plan, and the means. A misses the danger. C is a myth: asking doesn't plant the idea, and most patients feel relief. D delays help he may need today.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。长期抑郁后突然平静本身就是危险因素，「不会再麻烦大家多久」听起来像预警。他还丧偶、孤立。要直接、一步步地问念头、计划和手段。A 忽视了危险。C 是误区：问了不会让人起念头，多数病人反而松口气。D 拖延了他今天可能就需要的帮助。

slides.title: Caring for the suicidal patient
slides.body:
• Every threat or gesture is serious
  • Never leave them alone; quietly remove anything dangerous
  • Expect a last attempt before transport; protect yourself
  • Acknowledge feelings; don't argue with the wish to die
  • Bring pill bottles found on scene to hospital
  • Refuses? Ask family to help, then police
slides.say: Take every suicidal statement, gesture, or threat seriously. If someone phones threatening suicide, keep them on the line until crews arrive. On scene, quietly remove anything the patient could use, and never leave them alone. Some patients see the ambulance as their last chance and may try once more, or lash out at you, so protect yourself. Acknowledge their feelings, don't argue about the wish to die, and offer honest hope. Bring any pill bottles to the hospital. If they refuse to go, ask family or friends to help, then police. And after an attempt, the medical problem comes first.
slides.sayZh: 每一句自杀言语、每一个自杀姿态或威胁都要当真。如果有人打电话威胁要自杀，要一直保持通话直到救援到场。到场后悄悄移走病人可能用来自伤的东西，绝不让他独处。有些病人把救护车视为最后的机会，可能再试一次，或者攻击你，所以要保护好自己。承认他的感受，不和他争论求死的愿望，给予诚实的希望。把药瓶带到医院。如果拒绝去，先请家人或朋友帮忙劝，再不行就叫警察。而如果已经有过尝试，医疗问题优先。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: after an attempt
slides.body:
BC Suspected Narcotic Overdose, Diabetic Emergencies, Wound Care and Hypovolemia protocols

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Airway, BVM (two-person if needed), O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Vitals with BGL; correct a low sugar
  • Naloxone for the opioid picture
  • Bleeding: pressure, then tourniquet
  • Shock: supine, keep warm

PCP adds

  • Still unconscious + apneic: IV naloxone
  • Confirmed low sugar: D10W 10–25 g
  • Shock from blood loss: IV, 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Reassess every 500 mL; IV en route
slides.say: After an attempt, treat the medical problem first; BC protocols cover the common ones. On the left is what every licence level does: manage the airway and breathing, give oxygen to a saturation of ninety-four percent or higher, check the glucose and correct a low sugar, give naloxone for the opioid picture, and control bleeding with pressure and, if needed, a tourniquet. On the right is new. The PCP can give naloxone IV if the patient stays unconscious and apneic, gives D10W for confirmed low sugar, and for shock from blood loss starts an IV en route: twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred.
slides.sayZh: 有过尝试的病人，先处理医疗问题，BC 流程覆盖了常见情况。左栏是所有执照级别都做的：管理气道和呼吸，给氧使血氧维持在百分之九十四或以上，测血糖并纠正低血糖，对阿片类表现给纳洛酮，压迫止血，必要时上止血带。右栏是新的：病人持续昏迷且无呼吸时，PCP 可以静脉给纳洛酮；对确认的低血糖给 D10W；对失血性休克，在途中开静脉：每公斤二十毫升、最多两升、每五百毫升复评一次。

slides.title: Mania and psychosis
slides.body:
ManiaPsychosis
Looks likeeuphoric, no sleep, pressured speech, racing ideasdelusions, voices, odd or frozen behaviour
Dangercheer flips to anger fastvoices commanding harm
Approachcalm, firm, low stimulation, no sirenneutral distance; don't argue or play along
Watch forlithium toxicity: vomiting, slurred speech, tremormeth psychosis can last > 24 h
slides.say: A manic patient feels on top of the world: euphoric, barely sleeping, talking fast, jumping between ideas. The good mood can flip to anger in seconds, so stay calm and firm, don't argue, reduce noise, and transport without sirens. If they take lithium, vomiting, slurred speech, tremor, and drowsiness suggest toxicity, which needs a hospital. Psychosis means losing touch with reality, with delusions or voices. Keep a calm, neutral distance. Don't argue with the delusion and don't play along; if asked, simply say you don't hear the voice. Voices commanding harm to self or others make a patient dangerous.
slides.sayZh: 躁狂病人觉得自己好得不得了：欣快、几乎不睡、说话飞快、念头跳来跳去。好心情几秒钟就能翻成愤怒，所以要冷静、坚定，不争辩，减少噪音，转运时不鸣笛。如果病人服锂盐，出现呕吐、口齿不清、震颤和嗜睡提示锂中毒，需要去医院。精神病是脱离现实，有妄想或幻听。保持平静、中性的距离。不和妄想争辩，也不附和；被问到时，如实说你没听到那个声音。命令伤害自己或他人的幻听，意味着病人很危险。

slides.title: Spotting and defusing violence
slides.body:
• Risk: intoxication, withdrawal, psychosis, delirium (low sugar)
  • Warning signs: tense posture, loud threats, pacing, clenched fists
  • Keep two arm lengths, stand at 45°, never turn your back
  • Low voice; name the feeling; ask about weapons
  • Set limits: losing control isn't allowed
  • Armed, or words not working? Back off and call police
slides.say: Violence against paramedics is common: in a survey of one thousand six hundred seventy-six Canadian paramedics, seventy-five percent had faced workplace violence in the past twelve months. The highest-risk patients are intoxicated, in withdrawal, psychotic, or delirious from any cause, including low sugar or sepsis, so violence can be medical. Watch for tense posture, loud threats, pacing, clenched fists, and your own gut feeling. Keep two arm lengths away, stand at an angle, and never turn your back. Speak low, name the feeling, and ask directly about weapons. If there's a weapon or words aren't working, back off and call police.
slides.sayZh: 针对救护员的暴力很常见：一项对一千六百七十六名加拿大救护员的调查中，百分之七十五在过去十二个月里遭遇过职场暴力。风险最高的是醉酒或吸毒、戒断中、精神病发作，或任何原因导致谵妄的病人，包括低血糖或脓毒症，所以暴力也可能是医学问题。留意紧绷的姿态、大声威胁、来回踱步、握紧拳头，以及你自己的直觉。保持两臂长的距离，侧身站立，绝不背对病人。低声说话，说出对方的情绪，直接问有没有武器。如果有武器或语言无效，就后撤并叫警察。

slides.title: Physical restraint, done safely
slides.body:
• At least five trained people: one per limb, one for the head
  • One leader directs and keeps talking to the patient
  • Show of force first; remove your badge, scissors, keys
  • Secure supine, arms and legs to one side; head turns sideways

Never: face-down, wrists tied to ankles, feet-only (hobble) tie, prone on a Reeves stretcher → positional asphyxia
slides.say: When words fail, physical restraint may be needed, with police involved. This chapter asks for at least five trained people: one for each limb and one for the head, with one leader directing and talking to the patient. Chapter 4 called four the bare minimum, so plan for five. A show of force may be enough, so give the patient a way to back down. Secure the patient supine, arms and legs to one side, so the head turns sideways if they vomit. Never restrain face-down, never tie wrists to ankles or only the feet, and never lay them prone on a Reeves stretcher. These cause positional asphyxia, suffocation from body position.
slides.sayZh: 语言无效时可能需要身体约束，并要有警察参与。本章要求至少五名受过训练的人：每个肢体一人，头部一人，由一名指挥者指挥并与病人对话。第四章说四人是最低限度，所以按五人来计划。有时光是展示人手就够了，要给病人台阶下。让病人仰卧，双臂双腿固定在同一侧，这样万一呕吐，头会偏向一侧。绝不能俯卧约束，绝不能把手腕和脚踝绑在一起或只绑双脚，绝不能让病人俯卧在 Reeves 担架上。这些做法会导致体位性窒息，也就是因体位造成的窒息。

slides.q: Five responders have restrained an intoxicated, combative man supine on the stretcher. He suddenly goes quiet. What is your priority as the PCP?
options: Loosen the restraints to reward his cooperation
Reassess airway, breathing, vomiting and distal pulses right away
Turn him face-down so he can't kick if he wakes up
Give a benzodiazepine to keep him calm for the ride
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. Five responders have restrained an intoxicated, combative man supine on the stretcher. He suddenly goes quiet. What's your priority as the PCP? A, loosen the restraints to reward his cooperation. B, reassess his airway, breathing, vomiting, and distal pulses right away. C, turn him face-down so he can't kick if he wakes up. D, give a benzodiazepine to keep him calm for the ride. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。五名人员已把一名醉酒、有攻击性的男子仰卧约束在担架上。他突然安静下来。作为 PCP，你的首要任务是什么？A 松开约束，奖励他配合；B 立刻复评气道、呼吸、有无呕吐和远端脉搏；C 把他翻成俯卧，免得醒来后踢人；D 给苯二氮卓类让他一路保持安静。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Sudden quiet is not a reason to relax. An intoxicated patient can vomit, aspirate, or stop breathing, and tight restraints can cut off circulation, so check the airway, breathing, and radial and pedal pulses now. A is wrong: once restraints are on, you don't remove them or bargain. C risks positional asphyxia and makes monitoring hard. D is wrong for the exam: benzodiazepines aren't on the BC licensing exam.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。突然安静不是放松的理由。醉酒病人可能呕吐、误吸或停止呼吸，约束过紧还会阻断循环，所以要马上检查气道、呼吸以及桡动脉和足背动脉。A 错：约束一旦上了，就不解开、不讨价还价。C 有体位性窒息的风险，也难以监测。D 按考试也是错的：苯二氮卓类不在 BC 执照考试范围内。

slides.title: After restraint: monitor and document
slides.body:
• Watch airway, breathing, vomiting and circulation nonstop
  • Radial and dorsalis pedis pulses every few minutes
  • Keep talking; protect dignity; no deals, no removing
  • Suddenly calm does not mean safe
  • Record why (examples), team size, devices, ABCs and pulses after
  • TASER used? Look for the medical cause
slides.say: Once the patient is restrained, your job is close monitoring. Intoxication can turn violence into vomiting, aspiration, or slow breathing, so watch the airway, breathing, and circulation the whole time. Check the radial and dorsalis pedis pulses every few minutes; the book's case suggests every five minutes, with nerve function too. Don't remove restraints or bargain. Document why you restrained, with specific behaviours, how many people helped, the devices used, and the airway, breathing, and pulses afterward. And if police used a TASER, look for the medical cause behind the behaviour; police rely on you for that.
slides.sayZh: 病人被约束后，你的任务是密切监测。醉酒可能让暴力转为呕吐、误吸或呼吸变慢，所以全程盯住气道、呼吸和循环。每隔几分钟检查桡动脉和足背动脉；书中病例建议每五分钟一次，同时检查神经功能。不解开约束、不讨价还价。记录约束的理由并举出具体行为、参与人数、使用的器具，以及约束后的气道、呼吸和脉搏。如果警察用过泰瑟枪，要寻找行为背后的医学原因，警察要靠你来判断。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• "Panic" comes last: check SpO₂, BGL and the pulse first
  • Tricyclic antidepressants: dysrhythmias, dilated pupils, delirium
  • Lithium toxicity: vomiting, slurred speech, tremor → hospital
  • Overdose: ventilate, then naloxone; expect agitation
  • Restrained and intoxicated: watch for vomiting, slow breathing
  • Their drugs vs your drugs: think interactions
slides.say: Here's what's new at PCP level. Panic is a diagnosis you reach last: check the oxygen, the glucose, and the pulse first, and send every first attack to hospital. Know your patients' medications. Older tricyclic antidepressants can cause dysrhythmias, dilated pupils, and delirium. Lithium toxicity shows up as vomiting, slurred speech, tremor, and drowsiness. In an overdose, support breathing before naloxone, and expect withdrawal and agitation when it works. A restrained, intoxicated patient can vomit or stop breathing, so watch closely. And always think about how your drugs might interact with the drugs they already take.
slides.sayZh: 这些是 PCP 层面新要注意的。惊恐是最后才下的诊断：先查血氧、血糖和脉搏，所有首次发作都要送医。了解病人的用药：较老的三环类抗抑郁药可引起心律失常、瞳孔散大和谵妄；锂中毒表现为呕吐、口齿不清、震颤和嗜睡。过量时先保证通气再给纳洛酮，起效后要预料到戒断和躁动。被约束的醉酒病人可能呕吐或停止呼吸，要密切观察。还要时刻想到你的药物和病人已在服用的药物之间的相互作用。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Chemical restraint drugs: not on the BC licensing exam
  • Benzodiazepines: not on the exam
  • Haloperidol, droperidol, flumazenil: not BC exam drugs
  • Diphenhydramine: BC lists allergy and motion sickness, not dystonia
  • Naloxone: 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg IM/IV q3min, or 4 mg IN
slides.say: For the BC exam, be clear about what's tested. The textbook describes chemical restraint with benzodiazepines, haloperidol, droperidol, and newer antipsychotics. These aren't on the BC licensing exam, so on the exam, with a violent patient your tools are words, people, police, and safe physical restraint. Flumazenil, the book's benzodiazepine reversal drug, isn't a BC exam drug either. The book treats acute dystonia from older antipsychotics with IV diphenhydramine. Diphenhydramine is a BC PCP drug, but its listed BC uses are allergic reactions and motion sickness. And BC naloxone is zero point four, zero point four, zero point eight, then two milligrams, IM or IV, every three minutes, or four milligrams intranasal.
slides.sayZh: BC 考试要分清考什么。教科书讲了用苯二氮卓类、氟哌啶醇、氟哌利多和新型抗精神病药做化学约束。这些都不在 BC 执照考试范围内，所以考试中面对暴力病人，你的工具是语言、人手、警察和安全的身体约束。书中逆转苯二氮卓类的氟马西尼也不是 BC 考纲药物。书里用静脉苯海拉明处理老一代抗精神病药引起的急性肌张力障碍。苯海拉明在 BC 是 PCP 药物，但 BC 列出的用途是过敏反应和晕动病。BC 的纳洛酮是零点四、零点四、零点八、再二毫克，肌注或静注，每三分钟一次，或经鼻四毫克。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Ask about suicide directly, step by step; never leave the patient alone
  2. Medical first after an attempt: airway, naloxone, D10W, fluids per protocol
  3. Restrain with five, supine, never face-down; recheck breathing and pulses

Next: Chapter 41, Gynecologic Emergencies
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: ask about suicide directly and step by step; it doesn't plant the idea, and a past attempt, a plan, or suicide in the family means hospital assessment. Never leave that patient alone. Two: after an attempt, treat the medical problem first with your PCP tools: airway and ventilation, naloxone, D10W for confirmed low sugar, and fluids for shock from blood loss. Three: if you must restrain, use at least five people, secure the patient supine, never face-down, and keep checking breathing and pulses. Next time, Chapter 41, gynecologic emergencies. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，直接、一步步地问自杀问题；问了不会让人起念头。既往尝试、有计划或家族自杀史，都要送医院评估，而且绝不让这样的病人独处。二，有过尝试的病人，先用你的 PCP 工具处理医疗问题：气道与通气、纳洛酮、确认低血糖时给 D10W、失血性休克时补液。三，必须约束时，至少五人，仰卧固定，绝不俯卧，并不断复查呼吸和脉搏。下节课讲第四十一章，妇科急症。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
